prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory if capability<dispatch target; applies accepted ceiling). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; blocks protection conflicts; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace). Substation Operator: switching, clearances, confirms worksite switching understood; modes Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint. Grid Dispatcher: targets. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Work Permit Portal (Isolation Boundary Sketch), Personnel Tracking Console (crew list reconciled; entries/exits accounted), North/South Access Scanner (entry points), Operations Radio Console (radio test before teams split), Warehouse System. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy, Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note). Modes: Weather Hold (until operational authority clears), Vessel Standby. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum, Crew Count Correction; confirms positioning, transfer conditions. Service Operations Vessel (Recovery Basket Load Sheet); Crew Transfer Vessel. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation; berth conflicts by urgency, compatibility, delay; suspends access in unsafe sea/weather. Field Supervisor: cyber briefings; reviews limits; verifies worker authorization, competence, fitness; pauses job on deviation; handover briefing. Crew: boundaries match isolation/scope; PPE/comms/rescue checks; secure tools; listed personnel only, escorted visitors; scope change needs safety review; closeout after accounting, securing. Electrical Technician verifies isolation. HSE Officer checks emergency routes, muster. Cybersecurity Analyst (Firmware Hash Attestation; isolate only affected connection); SCADA Engineer validates restoration. Duty Planner: prioritizes, resources;

New part:
S516: The Control Engineer checks the current network configuration and confirms that the proposed sequence supports the approved work.
S517: The Substation Operator verifies equipment status and switching points at the Offshore Substation.
S518: The Grid Dispatcher confirms applicable grid requirements and any restrictions on changing the connection state.
S519: A Grid Constraint requires the Duty Planner to reassess the sequence and obtain revised authorization before work proceeds.
S520: The Maintenance Planning Engine provides the planned work period and identifies dependencies with other scheduled tasks.
S521: The Weather Service supplies forecast conditions relevant to access and safe execution.
S522: The Weather Analyst reviews the forecast and advises the Duty Planner if conditions could affect the planned sequence.
S523: The Marine Coordinator aligns vessel movements with the approved access plan and operational constraints.
S524: The Vessel Master confirms that the vessel can meet the agreed timing and maintain safe operating margins.
S525: The Personnel Tracking Console and Work Permit Portal are checked to confirm that assigned personnel and permits are ready.
S526: The HSE Officer reviews task hazards and confirms that required controls are in place before switching is authorized.
S527: The Duty Planner records the proposed sequence, required approvals, execution roles, and planned communications in the operating record.
S528: The Control Engineer prepares clear switching instructions with one action per step and an explicit hold point where needed.
S529: The Electrical Technician verifies equipment labels and confirms the intended switching points before execution.
S530: The Substation Operator accepts the instructions only after checking the equipment state and confirming authorization with the Control Engineer.
S531: The Shore Control Room sends the Switching Window Acknowledgment after the approved switching period is entered in the operating log.
S532: The Substation Operator uses the test trace to verify that the planned restoration checks have completed before requesting the next switching step.
S533: During execution, the switching operator performs each authorized action and reports completion before the next instruction is issued.
S534: The Control Engineer monitors available indications and confirms that each reported state change matches the approved sequence.
S535: If an indication is ambiguous, communications fail, or conditions differ from the plan, the sequence is paused and the equipment is left in a safe state.
S536: The Field Supervisor confirms personnel are clear of affected equipment before the Duty Planner authorizes restoration or release of the work area.
S537: After completion, the Duty Planner records the final equipment state, approvals, deviations, and handover information for the incoming shift.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
